What are primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl amines?
modelAnswer: A primary amine has one alkyl group on nitrogen (RNH2), a secondary has two (R2NH), and a tertiary has three (R3N).
Amines are organic derivatives of ammonia in which one or more hydrogen atoms are replaced by alkyl or aryl groups.

stem: Identify the differences between different types of amines in terms of their structures and chemical properties.
keyPoints: ["Primary (RNH2), secondary (R2NH) and tertiary (R3N) amines differ in the number of alkyl substituents on nitrogen.","Basicity, boiling point (via hydrogen bonding capacity) and reactivity towards electrophiles vary systematically with the degree of substitution: primary and secondary amines can hydrogen-bond via N-H, tertiary amines cannot."]

stem: Make a comparison between primary amines and secondary amines.
keyPoints: ["Primary amines (RNH2) have one alkyl group and two N-H bonds; secondary amines (R2NH) have two alkyl groups and one N-H bond.","Both can hydrogen-bond and act as nucleophiles/bases, but secondary amines are generally slightly more basic in solution (more electron-donating alkyl groups), while primary amines have somewhat higher boiling points from stronger hydrogen bonding (two N-H donors)."]

stem: Amines have higher melting/boiling points compared to analogous alkanes. Why?
modelAnswer: Primary and secondary amines can form hydrogen bonds (N-H...N) between molecules, requiring more energy to separate them than the weak van der Waals forces in alkanes of similar molecular mass.

stem: How can ethylamine be prepared from: a) an alkyl halide b) a nitrite c) an amide
modelAnswer: Ethylamine can be prepared from: a) Alkyl halide: Ethyl halide (C₂H₅X) reacts with ammonia (NH₃) via nucleophilic substitution ($S_N$) to form ethylamine: $C_2H_5X + 2NH_3 \rightarrow C_2H_5NH_2 + NH_4X$. b) Nitrite: Ethyl nitrite (C₂H₅ONO) undergoes reduction with reducing agents like LiAlH₄ or Sn/HCl to produce ethylamine: $C_2H_5ONO + [H] \rightarrow C_2H_5NH_2$. c) Amide: Ethanamide (CH₃CONH₂) is reduced using LiAlH₄ or Sn/HCl, where the carbonyl group is reduced to CH₂, forming ethylamine: $CH_3CONH_2 + [H] \rightarrow C_2H_5NH_2$.

Explain why amines are more basic than ammonia.
modelAnswer: Alkyl groups are electron-donating (+I effect), increasing the electron density on nitrogen and making the lone pair more available to accept a proton than in ammonia.

stem: Methylamine is a stronger base than ammonia. Explain.
modelAnswer: The methyl group in methylamine donates electron density to nitrogen (+I effect), increasing the availability of the lone pair and making it a stronger base than ammonia.
